data.title: Mapping the placental galectin-3 interactome identifies CD9 and ITGB1 as functional glycoprotein counter-receptors during syncytialization.
data.projectDescription: The fetomaternal interface is replete with glycan-binding proteins (GBPs) that can interact with cell surface glycoprotein counter-receptors to regulate placental function. Here, we interrogate the role of galectin-3, a GBP that controls placental trophoblast syncytialization, an important differentiation process where progenitor cytotrophoblast cells fuse to produce the multinucleated syncytiotrophoblast. The molecular mechanism of galectin-3-mediated fusion has not yet been elucidated in part due to the difficulty of studying glycan-GBP binding events in live cells. To overcome these challenges, we employ a proximity labeling strategy to identify the galectin-3 interactome. From this interactome dataset, we selected and validated CD9 and integrin beta 1 as functional counter-receptors of galectin-3 and showed that CD9 is glycosylated with an N-linked glycan at a rare non-canonical sequon. Furthermore, we present evidence that galectin-3 acts to physically alter the fluidity of the cellular membrane and it does not activate canonical syncytialization signaling pathways. Overall, we report that galectin-mediated binding events and their corresponding functions in cell biology can be precisely regulated by select glycoproteins at specific glycosites.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Sample preparation for PX-Gal-3 MS-based proteomics Cells scraped on ice were pelleted (500 xg, 3 min, 4°C) and lysed in cold PBS with Branson SFX250 sonicator (15 ms on, 40 ms off, 1 s total on time, 15% amplitude). Protein quantification was performed with DC™ Protein Assay Kit II with a BSA standard curve. Samples were normalized (500 µg, 1 mg/mL) and protein precipitated with methanol (2 mL, O/N, -20°C). Protein was pelleted (3260 xg, 10 min, 4°C) and washed with methanol (1 mL) after sonication to resuspend completely. Protein was pelleted (3260 xg, 10 min, 4°C) then denatured (500 µl 6 M urea in PBS, 10 µl 10% SDS), reduced (50 µl of premixed 200 mM TCEP in PBS and 600 mM K2CO3 in PBS, 30 min, 37°C shaking), and alkylated (70 µl 400 mM iodoacetamide in PBS, 30 min, RT, in dark). Samples were quenched (5.5 mL PBS, 130 µl 10% SDS) then enriched on prewashed streptavidin-agarose beads (1.5 h, RT, rotating). Beads were pelleted (2000 rpm, 2 min, RT) then washed successively with 0.2% SDS in PBS, PBS, and 100 mM TEAB in water (pH 8.5). Beads were transferred to low-bind Eppendorf tubes (Fisher Scientific, 13-698-794) 100 mM TEAB (pH 8.5) and pelleted (2000 rpm, 2 min, RT). Samples were subjected to tryptic digest (2 µg of procine trypsin in 200 µl 100 mM TEAB (pH 8.5), 1 mM CaCl2, O/N, 37°C, shaking). Beads were pelleted (2000 rpm, 5 min, RT) and supernatant carefully retained in new low-bind tube. Beads were washed with 100 µl 100 mM TEAB (pH 8.5) and pelleted (2000, 5 min, RT) to ensure complete transfer of tryptic peptides. Samples were brought to 30% acetonitrile and combined with respective TMT10plex™ Isobaric Label (Thermo Scientific, 90110) (1 h, 37°C, occasional vortex). Reaction was quenched (6 µl 5% hydroxylamine in water, 15 min, RT) and acidified (4 µl formic acid). Samples were dried by vacuum concentration and reconstituted/combined in 5% acetonitrile, 0.5% TFA in water. Samples were desalted with PierceTM Peptide Desalting Spin Columns per manufacturer protocol then dried by vacuum concentration. Samples were stored at -80°C until resuspended in 20 μl of 0.1 % formic acid in water (Buffer A) and loaded onto instrument.  Liquid Chromatography (LC) and synchronous precursor selection (SPS)-MS3 method for proteomics LC was performed with nEasy LC1000 nano liquid chromatography system (Thermo Scientific™) and on-line eluted into a Fusion Tribrid mass spectrometer from EASY PepMapTM RSLC C18 column (3% Buffer B – 80% acetonitrile in water, 0.1% formic acid, 10 min hold). Buffer B gradient was adjusted (3 to 38% over 192 min, 38 to 75% over 5 min, 100% hold over 5 min, 100 to 4% over 1 min, 4% hold over 6 min). EASY spray source was set to 50°C and 1.9 kV for ionization (250 nL/min flow). SPS-MS3 scanning (345 to 1500 m/z) at a resolution of 120,000 for MS1 at automatic gain control (AGC) target of 1E5 with maximum injection time of 50 msec was performed in the Orbitrap mass analyzer. Collision-induced dissociation (30% energy) was performed for peptide monoisotopic ions with a charge 2 to 8 and above intensity threshold (5E3) using quadrupole isolation of 1.6 m/z. AGC target of 1.8E4 with maximum injection time of 120 msec was set for ion trap. The dynamic exclusion duration S5 was set to 20 sec with ions excluded after 1 time within +/- 10 ppm mass tolerance. The top ten MS2 ions present between 400 to 1200 m/z were subjected to higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) (65%) for MS3. Orbitrap detection occurred with resolution 50,000 AGC target 1E5, 120 msec injection time, 3 sec specified cycle time for all scan events. Methods were based on Ting et al.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: Quantification and statistical analyses MS-based proteomics experiments were designed with three replicates of 100 nM PX-Gal-3, two replicates of 100 nM PX-Gal-3 with 100 mM lactose, and two replicates of 0 nM PX-Gal-3. Data were processed in Proteome Discoverer v 2.5 (Thermo Scientific™) with the SEQUEST HT homo sapiens sequence database (42,358 proteins). Search allowed for one missed trypsin cleavage site, fixed modifications of carbamidomethyl cysteines and TMT10plex of lysines and N-terminus, and variable modifications of oxidation. Fragment ion mass tolerance was 0.6 Da, and the mass tolerance was 10 ppm with a 1 % FDR. Identified proteins were filtered for greater than or equal to two unique peptides. All keratins were removed from the dataset. GraphPad Prism software was used to perform statistical analysis on quantified proteins with abundance values converted to log2(Y). Statistical comparisons between conditions were performed with an unpaired student’s t test with the average fold change (x-axis) and p-value (y-axis) presented as a volcano plot. Significance was determined for comparisons with a p-value less than 0.05, equating to values greater than 1.30 on the -log(p-value) scale. Two proteomics experiments were performed with the significantly enriched and competed proteins shared by both MS-based proteomics experiments reported with the individual and average enrichment and competition scores (Supplemental Data).
